The selected tensor component, collapsed sums, gamma-v factor, and charge-rest-frame interpretation answer the opening puzzle.

entries.note: Particle equations are distinguished from field equations, and eight scalar equations are packaged as four vector equations.

entries.note: Definitions, cyclic permutations, commuting derivatives, and both classroom polls are preserved.

entries.note: Divergence of a curl gives zero, while the later qualification about magnetic monopoles is retained.

entries.locator: Faraday equation from the electric potential
entries.note: The curl of the electric potential relation is worked through and the homogeneous pair is assembled.
Gauss's law, the Ampere-Maxwell equation, rho, current density, and the deferred action derivation remain together.
The neighboring-board observation, mathematics-faculty course, frustration question, and return to the subject are preserved.
A fixed-time spatial cell cuts particle worldlines and defines charge per volume.
The window orientation, ceiling correction, signs, and all three spatial currents are retained.
Time-normal and spatially normal fluxes are assembled into a contravariant four-vector.
Horizon litter, redshift, fading, Hawking background, huge wavelengths, crossing time, and evaporation rate remain in order.
The Alpha Centauri and Coma examples motivate why fixed total charge is weaker than local conservation.
Opposite-face currents produce the three divergence terms and the local balance equation.
The sourced equations imply continuity, and Maxwell's time-dependent addition is identified as essential.
The four derivatives are contracted and the partial-time-derivative question is resolved.
The Bianchi identity is written and its all-spatial component gives divergence B.
The class chooses the time index, Faraday's equation is recovered, and the second-derivative proof and spelling exchange follow.
Repeated indices, permutations, 24 distinct-index orderings, and four independent equations are distinguished.
The electric-magnetic quarter-turn, time-space question, source rotation, and monopole formulation close the lecture.
The right-hand-rule direction depends on charge sign and axis orientation.
Magnetic components occupy the purely spatial tensor block.
The off-diagonal signs are corrected before transformation.
The previous result governed a particle in a prescribed field, not the field itself.
Eight scalar components are conventionally packaged as four equations.

entries.locator: Who finds the teaching assignment frustrating
entries.note: The challenge is acknowledged on both sides of the physics-mathematics exchange.
A yz window is normal to x regardless of the room analogy.
Charge density and three currents are four orientations of one flux.
The current is introduced contravariantly and lowered with the metric when needed.
Coordinate-time slowing is separated from the rapidly fading received signal.
The distant description and quantum radiation are distinguished.
Practical signal loss occurs much earlier, and the crossing-time estimate is retained.

entries.locator: Evaporation rate over the black-hole lifetime
entries.note: Shrinking radius, increasing temperature, and accelerating emission are stated consistently.
Their action derivation is deferred and the displacement-current role is identified.

entries.locator: Partial versus total derivative of rho
entries.note: The density changes in a fixed box rather than along a moving trajectory.
The name and deferred geometric significance are retained.
Repeated indices vanish and permutations repeat four independent triples.
The correct source-free operation is a signed quarter-turn in the E-B plane.
A monopole requires patchwise, singular-gauge, or dual-potential treatment.
All tensor signs follow one declared mostly-plus convention while preserving the lecture's sign-agnostic physical conclusion.
The spatial source sign is fixed by the covariant equation and continuity; the live correction is documented in Lecture 9.
The shrinking hole heats up, emits faster, and has a shorter characteristic wavelength.
One global smooth potential is replaced by patchwise or singular gauge descriptions.
